reviews.comment: There are guest speakers and reflection hw every week. A few assignments here and there, but I spent maybe 2 hrs. max per week outside of class. Would have been useful if I was a freshman/sophomore but they're opening it up to lower undergrad so lucky y'all. Overall, very easy & highly recommend if you want to explore outside of pre-health careers!

Overall, I have really enjoyed this class. The professor is very passionate about what he lectures and he is easy to understand. I took a lot of notes during his lectures, but he does post the lectures online beforehand. Expect to prepare well for the exams by memorizing the slides and drawing the pertinent diagrams. Previous exams are helpful.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Although Dr. Lockless cares about his students, the exams are extremely difficult, and many times the questions being asked are unclear which makes the exams even WORSE. He does provide previous exams that may be used while studying; however, the previous exams are not always representative of how the TRUE exam will be.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Lockless is an extremely kind professor, but his tests are HARD. The exam is either identical to a practice test or nothing like it. This class is NOT curved and graded by 4 exams and a group project alone. Exams are all free response and graded by a TA, not him. Chance to 'challenge' test questions, this is the only points you'll get back.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Lockless is a friendly, young, relatable professor. He was an absolute pleasure to talk to inside and outside of class. He truly cares about his students and the research he does, and it shows during lecture. One of my favorite things about him was his lack of ego, he would always admit if he didn't know the answer to a question. AWESOME CLASS!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved this class. Dr. L is a great lecturer. He is friendly, approachable, and extremely knowledgable. Honors section was very engaging w/ small class. Fall 2017: no book reading, no hw, 4 tests, and final project. I made A by studying 30 minutes b4 every class, 10 hrs spread out over the weekend b4 test, and went to SI review for test.

Lockless is an amazing prof - the kind who pauses lecture to say "bless you" and whose face lights up with a huge smile when teaching something he thinks is cool. An A didn't require a ton of work (even for honors) bc his expectations are so clear. Textbook is unnecessary - if you know the info on the powerpoints you will be set for tests.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: I respect Dr. Lockless as a professor. He is a good at keeping the class engaged in his lectures and explaining concepts. He welcomes questions, and shows he cares about the students. However, he is very difficult; one of the toughest professors I've had. Exams are about 1/3 multiple choice, the rest are short answer/diagram questions. DON'T TAKE!!

He's a very good teacher. I would take another class from him. He explains things in different ways to help us understand. If you don't answer in class he will wait until you do, so don't be afraid to throw your thoughts out there.

Took him for Fall '14, had to drop. Never dropped any upper level courses before at A&M and I'm a junior.  Taught along side Gomer, who was worse than him. Wait until Spring to take this course, you should stay away from this duo unless you want to suffer. TAKE SOMEONE ELSE!! I don't know how else to say it, but I'll reiterate, DON'T TAKE HIM!

Tests are extremely hard and free response is usually 50-75 points of it. If you don't write exactly what he wants he won't give you credit. Super nice guy and willing to help if you go to office hours. Nice to look at as well.

Tests are tough and you really have to know ALL the material. Studying amount reflected in your grade. Study learning objectives a lot before the test. Really know all material. Tests are part short answer, part MC. Tough material, but achievable.

I didn't have the chance of selecting my professor for this class, and he was assigned to me due to being a transfer student. He goes way too fast! His excuse? "You should already know this". His tests are HARD, and you must read everything in the textbook because he tests out of it. His lectures are NOT clear at all. Please avoid if you can!
